intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the bustling 36 streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter on foot, sampling iconic street foods like Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Stay in a hostel within the Old Quarter itself to maximize time and minimize travel. Since the flight arrives late on Day 1, this activity is perfectly suited for Day 2 morning when energy is restored and the quarter comes alive with breakfast vendors.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival and Night Market
experiences.description: Wander through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, visiting tailor shops, temples, and the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge. As evening falls, join the monthly Lantern Festival or browse the vibrant night market for cheap local eats like Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings. Book a budget guesthouse on Tran Phu Street to be steps away from all activity hubs, avoiding wasted transit time.

experiences.name: Hue Imperial Citadel and Royal Tomb Bicycle Tour
experiences.description: Rent a bicycle from your centrally located guesthouse near Dong Ba Market and cycle to the Imperial Citadel, the Forbidden Purple City, and the ornate Royal Tombs of the Nguyen Dynasty. This self-guided backpacker-friendly tour immerses you in Vietnam's imperial history at minimal cost. Staying near the citadel area ensures no time is lost on long commutes, especially important given the late arrival on Day 1.

experiences.name: Ho Chi Minh City War Remnants Museum and Ben Thanh Street Food
experiences.description: Visit the powerful War Remnants Museum in District 3 to gain deep insight into Vietnam's modern history, then walk to the Ben Thanh Market area for an afternoon of street food including Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes), fresh spring rolls, and sugarcane juice. Choose a hostel in District 1 or District 3 to keep both attractions within easy walking distance, making the most of every day without wasting time on transport.
experiences.location: District 3 and Ben Thanh, Ho Chi Minh City

experiences.name: Ninh Binh Tam Coc Boat Ride and Countryside Cycling
experiences.description: Take a budget day trip or overnight stay to Ninh Binh, often called 'Halong Bay on land.' Glide through limestone karsts and rice paddies on a traditional rowboat at Tam Coc, then rent a bicycle to explore Bich Dong Pagoda and the ancient capital of Hoa Lu. Stay at a guesthouse in Ninh Binh town to be within 5 minutes of the boat docks, avoiding the common mistake of booking accommodation far from the activity hub.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the 86 airport bus (~45 min, ~45,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check in to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, freshen up, and take a slow walk around Hoan Kiem Lake to shake off jet lag. Admire Ngoc Son Temple on the lake and get your bearings in the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the famous Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Fri-Sun) or stroll Ta Hien Street — known as 'Beer Street' — for cheap bia hoi (fresh draught beer at ~10,000 VND per glass). Watch the world go by from a tiny plastic stool.

meals.breakfast: N/A - in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick Banh Mi from a street cart near the Old Quarter for ~25,000 VND upon arrival
meals.dinner: Bun Cha (grilled pork with noodles) at a local Old Quarter eatery such as Bun Cha Huong Lien (~60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or use a local ATM (Vietcombank has low fees). Avoid taxi touts — use the official airport bus or book a Grab (ride-hailing app). Keep your accommodation address written in Vietnamese to show drivers.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a street-side Pho breakfast near the hotel. Head to Hoan Kiem Lake for morning tai chi watching (locals gather 6:00–7:30 AM). Cross the red Huc Bridge to visit Ngoc Son Temple (~30,000 VND entry). Walk through the 36 Streets of the Old Quarter, each named after the guild that once traded there — spot Hang Bac (silver), Hang Gai (silk), and Hang Ma (paper goods).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — Vietnam's first university, founded in 1070 (~30,000 VND entry, ~20 min by Grab). Explore its five courtyards and ancient stone steles. Walk to the nearby Fine Arts Museum (~40,000 VND) to see Vietnamese lacquerware, sculpture, and war-era propaganda art.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter and visit Dong Xuan Market — Hanoi's largest covered market — for cheap souvenirs and local snacks. Dinner in the market area. End the night with a Bia Hoi on Ta Hien Street.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) from a street stall near the hotel (~40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) from a local stall near Temple of Literature (~35,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Com Binh Dan (budget rice dish with multiple toppings) at Dong Xuan Market area (~50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Old Quarter streets are uneven. Bargain respectfully at markets; start at 50% of the asking price. The Temple of Literature is one of Hanoi's most photogenic spots — go before 10 AM to beat the crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (free entry, open Tue–Thu & Sat–Sun mornings, closed Mon & Fri). See the embalmed Ho Chi Minh, the Presidential Palace, and his simple stilt house. Dress respectfully (covered shoulders and knees). Nearby, visit the One Pillar Pagoda — a iconic single-column lotus-shaped temple (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND, ~10 min by Grab from Ba Dinh area) — one of Southeast Asia's best ethnology museums, showcasing Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups with outdoor reconstructed traditional houses. Spend 2–3 hours here.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the Old Quarter. Watch the Hoan Kiem Lake light up at dusk. Try egg coffee (Ca Phe Trung) at the original Cafe Giang on Nguyen Huu Huan Street — a Hanoi institution (~30,000 VND). Browse the night market if it's a weekend.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street cart near the hotel (~25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodle salad) from a stall near the Museum of Ethnology (~45,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric fish with dill) — splurge slightly at a local restaurant (~120,000–150,000 VND) — this is Hanoi's signature dish

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays, and for about 2 months each year for maintenance (usually Sep–Nov). Check official schedules. Photography inside the mausoleum is strictly prohibited. Arrive before 10 AM to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station to Ninh Binh (~2.5 hours, ~80,000–100,000 VND). Arrive and rent a bicycle (~50,000–70,000 VND/day) from your guesthouse. Cycle to Tam Coc and board a sampan boat ride (~150,000 VND) through stunning limestone karst scenery and rice paddies — often called 'Ha Long Bay on land.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda (free) carved into the limestone cliffs — climb to the upper cave for panoramic views. Continue to Thung Nham Bird Garden or simply cycle through the scenic countryside villages around Tam Coc.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a budget guesthouse in Ninh Binh town or Tam Coc (~150,000–200,000 VND/night). Explore the local night market and eat dinner at a riverside restaurant. Ninh Binh is famous for its goat meat dishes.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure in Hanoi — Banh Mi from a street cart (~25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice) or Bun (noodles) at a local Tam Coc eatery (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: De Nuong (grilled goat) — Ninh Binh's specialty — at a local restaurant (~80,000–120,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat ride early as slots fill up. Boat ladies may try to sell you embroidery mid-river — politely decline if not interested. Bring sunscreen and a hat as the boat ride is fully exposed. This is a full day trip so pack light and bring a day bag.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike or motorbike (~50,000 VND rental) to Mua Cave (Hang Mua) — climb ~500 steps to the dragon spine ridge for the most spectacular panoramic view of the Tam Coc rice fields and karst mountains (~100,000 VND entry). Best in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hoa Lu Ancient Capital (entry ~20,000 VND) — Vietnam's 10th-century capital with two ancient temples dedicated to King Dinh and King Le. Then head to the bus station and take a sleeper bus south to Hue (~200,000–250,000 VND, approximately 10–12 hours overnight).
day_by_day.evening: Board the overnight sleeper bus to Hue. Get comfortable on your bunk bed berth — a quintessential backpacker experience in Vietnam. The bus departs around 6–8 PM.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Chao (rice porridge) at the guesthouse or a local stall (~35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Banh Mi or Com Binh Dan near Hoa Lu (~40,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Quick meal at the bus station before boarding (~50,000 VND) or bring snacks for the overnight journey

day_by_day.notes: Book your sleeper bus ticket at least 1 day in advance — ask your guesthouse to help. Bring an eye mask, earplugs, and a light layer as buses can be cold from AC. Store valuables in your day bag under your bunk. The Mua Cave climb is steep but very rewarding.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Hue in the early morning. Check into a budget hostel in the city centre (~120,000–180,000 VND/night). After freshening up, head to Hue's Imperial Citadel (Dai Noi) — the walled palace complex of the Nguyen Dynasty (~200,000 VND entry). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Forbidden Purple City, royal palaces, and ornate gates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) and cycle along the Perfume River to visit the Thien Mu Pagoda (free) — Hue's most iconic seven-storey pagoda with sweeping river views. Continue cycling to explore the tombs of the Nguyen emperors (Minh Mang or Tu Duc Tomb, ~100,000 VND each) set in peaceful forested grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and explore Hue's famous street food scene at Dong Ba Market or the backpacker area near Pham Ngu Lao Street. Hue is the culinary capital of Vietnam — don't miss its unique royal cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Hue or Chao (rice porridge) near the hostel (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup) — the city's most famous dish at a local stall (~40,000–55,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Com Hen (baby clam rice) and Banh Khoai (crispy sizzling pancake) at Dong Ba Market (~60,000–80,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Hue's Imperial Citadel is large — wear comfortable shoes and bring water. The bicycle ride along the Perfume River is one of Vietnam's most scenic urban rides. Hue cuisine is distinctly different from Hanoi and Saigon — try as many local dishes as possible. The city can be rainy (central Vietnam weather is unpredictable), so pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or book a shared minivan to Hoi An (~3–4 hours, ~100,000–150,000 VND). The route crosses the spectacular Hai Van Pass — if budget allows, consider renting a motorbike or joining a motorbike tour for this stretch for unforgettable coastal mountain views (~200,000–300,000 VND). Arrive in Hoi An by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a budget guesthouse in Hoi An (~150,000–200,000 VND/night). Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) and explore Hoi An Ancient Town (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Visit the Japanese Covered Bridge (entry included in the Ancient Town ticket ~120,000 VND), Chinese Assembly Halls, and the old merchant houses. The town is compact and beautifully preserved.
day_by_day.evening: Hoi An comes alive at night with colourful lanterns reflected in the Thu Bon River. Buy a paper lantern (~20,000 VND) and release it on the river. Explore the night market on An Hoi Island for street food and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure from Hue — Banh Mi (~25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish) at a local restaurant in the Ancient Town (~55,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Banh Mi Phuong — Hoi An's famous banh mi stall (~30,000–50,000 VND total) at the night market

day_by_day.notes: The Ancient Town ticket covers entry to 5 heritage sites — choose wisely based on your interests. Many tailors in Hoi An offer custom clothing at budget prices (allow 24–48 hours for tailoring). The town is best explored by bicycle — avoid tuk-tuks which charge tourist prices. Tuesday is the Lantern Festival night when the town turns off electric lights — magical if your dates align.

day_by_day.morning: Cycle 4 km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach — Hoi An's closest beaches. Spend the morning swimming and relaxing. Beach chairs are often free if you buy a drink from a beach shack (~30,000–50,000 VND). Alternatively, join a free cooking class intro session offered by some guesthouses, or visit the local Hoi An Central Market for a vibrant morning food scene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tra Que Vegetable Village (~3 km from town by bicycle, ~20,000 VND entry) — a charming organic farming village where you can participate in gardening and cooking activities. Then cycle back through rice fields to town. Explore the craft workshops along Le Loi Street — watch lantern makers, silk weavers, and wood carvers at work.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short boat trip on the Thu Bon River (~50,000–80,000 VND) at sunset. Dine at a local restaurant away from the tourist centre for better prices. Spend the evening strolling the lantern-lit Ancient Town one more time.

meals.breakfast: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with pork and shrimp) at a local stall (~40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a beach shack at An Bang Beach (~80,000–120,000 VND for grilled fish or prawns)
meals.dinner: Com Ga Hoi An (Hoi An chicken rice) at a local eatery off the tourist strip (~45,000–60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An is extremely popular — book accommodation in advance. The beaches can be crowded on weekends. Tra Que Village is a wonderful off-the-beaten-path experience. If you want to take a cooking class, book a budget option (~200,000–300,000 VND) that includes a market visit — great cultural immersion.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus or sleeper bus to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) — approximately 16–20 hours by bus (~250,000–350,000 VND) or consider a budget flight (~500,000–800,000 VND on VietJet or Bamboo Airways booked in advance). If flying, head to Da Nang Airport (~30 km from Hoi An, ~150,000 VND by Grab). Arrive in HCMC in the afternoon or evening depending on transport choice.
day_by_day.afternoon: If taking the bus: settle in and enjoy the coastal scenery. If flying: arrive Da Nang, fly to Tan Son Nhat Airport HCMC, take bus 109 to the city centre (~20,000 VND). Check into a budget hostel in the Bui Vien backpacker district or District 1 (~120,000–180,000 VND/night).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Bui Vien Walking Street — HCMC's famous backpacker strip with cheap beer, street food, and live music. Visit Ben Thanh Night Market nearby for street food and souvenirs. Grab a Saigon Special beer (~15,000 VND) from a street vendor and soak up the electric energy of Vietnam's largest city.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from Hoi An before departure (~25,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Snacks and instant noodles on the bus, or airport food if flying (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes) and Goi Cuon (fresh spring rolls) at a street stall on Bui Vien (~60,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Budget flights between Da Nang and HCMC are often cheaper than the bus when booked in advance — check VietJet, Bamboo, and Vietnam Airlines. If taking the overnight bus, book a sleeper bus (giuong nam) for comfort. The Bui Vien area is very lively but can be overwhelming — keep an eye on your belongings in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — one of the most powerful and sobering museums in Southeast Asia, documenting the Vietnam War through photographs and artefacts. Allow 2 hours. Walk to the nearby Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) — the former South Vietnamese presidential palace frozen in time since 1975, complete with war-era bunkers and command rooms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore District 1's street food scene around Ben Thanh Market. Browse the market for last-minute souvenirs (bargain hard). Walk or take a Grab to the Jade Emperor Pagoda (free) — an atmospheric Taoist temple filled with incense smoke and intricate carvings. End the afternoon with a wander through the colourful Cho Lon Chinatown area in District 5 (~15 min by Grab).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Bui Vien area for a final Vietnamese feast. Reflect on your 10-day journey over a bia hoi. If departing tonight, head to Tan Son Nhat Airport (bus 109 from city centre, ~20,000 VND). If staying another night, enjoy a rooftop bar for farewell drinks with city views.

meals.breakfast: Hu Tieu (Southern-style noodle soup) from a street cart near the hostel (~40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork, egg, and pickles) — HCMC's iconic dish at a local com tam stall (~55,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Lau (Vietnamese hot pot) shared with fellow travellers at a budget restaurant on Bui Vien (~100,000–150,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense — allow time to process what you see. Com Tam is best at local neighbourhood stalls away from tourist areas. Keep airport transfer time in mind — Tan Son Nhat can have heavy traffic; allow 90 minutes from the city centre during peak hours. Vietnam requires no visa for many nationalities for stays under 45 days — verify your status before travel.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel in the Old Quarter (approximately 45 minutes by taxi or Grab app, ~200,000 VND). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle first explore of the Old Quarter on foot. Stroll the famous 36 Ancient Streets, browse silk shops and lantern stalls, and visit Hoan Kiem Lake and the iconic red Huc Bridge leading to Ngoc Son Temple (entrance ~30,000 VND). Take in the atmosphere and get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Hanoi Old Quarter Night Market (open Fri–Sun) on Hang Dao Street for souvenir browsing and street food grazing. Watch local life unfold around Hoan Kiem Lake as locals exercise and socialize. Early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha Huong Lien (near Old Quarter) — the famous spot where Anthony Bourdain dined. Grilled pork with rice noodles and broth, ~60,000–80,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Pho Thin on Dinh Tien Hoang Street — a Hanoi institution for beef pho. Bowl costs ~60,000–80,000 VND. Simple, authentic, perfect for a tired traveler.

day_by_day.notes: Use Grab (Vietnam's Uber equivalent) for all taxi rides — always safer and cheaper than unlicensed taxis. Exchange some cash at the airport or an ATM in the Old Quarter. Keep your first evening light to adjust to the time zone.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the quintessential Hanoi breakfast experience at a local café on a narrow Old Quarter alley. Then visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex (check opening hours — usually 7:30–10:30 AM, closed Mon/Fri). See the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's stilt house, and the One Pillar Pagoda (~40,000 VND combined entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (entry ~40,000 VND) — one of Southeast Asia's best museums, showcasing 54 ethnic groups with outdoor reconstructed village houses. Take a cyclo or Grab back to the Old Quarter afterward. Browse Hang Gai Street (Silk Street) for quality Vietnamese lacquerware and ao dai.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre on Dinh Tien Hoang (~100,000–200,000 VND). Book tickets in advance online. Afterward, explore the buzzing Ta Hien Street (Beer Corner) for a cold Bia Hoi (draft beer, ~10,000–15,000 VND per glass).

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi 25 on Hang Ca Street — legendary Vietnamese baguette sandwiches, ~35,000–50,000 VND. Eat standing on the street like a local.
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Nam Bo near Hang Dieu Street — dry beef noodle salad bowl, fresh and flavorful, ~60,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong on Cha Ca Street — Hanoi's iconic turmeric-marinated fish dish cooked at your table with dill and spring onions, ~200,000–250,000 VND per person. A must-try cultural dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays and during the October–November maintenance period. Dress respectfully (covered shoulders and knees). Water puppet shows sell out — book 1 day ahead online or at the box office in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh (2 hours by bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat station, ~100,000 VND). Arrive and rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) to explore the Tam Coc area. Take a 2-hour rowing boat trip through Tam Coc's limestone karst caves and rice paddies (~150,000 VND) — often called 'Ha Long Bay on land.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda (free entry, small tip for monk), a stunning cave pagoda carved into a limestone cliff. Continue cycling through lush green rice fields to Hoa Lu Ancient Capital — Vietnam's 10th-century capital with two historic temples (~20,000 VND entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus or booked minivan (~120,000 VND). Arrive back in the Old Quarter by 7–8 PM. Unwind with a walk around Hoan Kiem Lake lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Com Pho 49 on Bat Dan Street — traditional Hanoi rice porridge (chao) with century egg and pork, ~40,000 VND, before catching the bus.
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Tam Coc village — try Com Nieu (clay pot rice) with fresh goat meat (de nui), a Ninh Binh specialty, ~100,000–150,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Quan An Ngon on Phan Boi Chau Street, Hanoi — a beautiful courtyard restaurant with stalls serving dishes from all over Vietnam. Budget ~150,000–200,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book a day trip or organize transport independently — a self-organized trip is cheaper. Bring sunscreen and a hat; cycling in April can be warm and sunny. Start early (7 AM bus) to maximize time in Ninh Binh.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an overnight or early morning train/bus to Hue (approximately 13–14 hours by train, or fly for ~500,000–800,000 VND on VietJet/Bamboo). If flying, take the 6–7 AM flight to Phu Bai Airport. Check into a mid-range guesthouse in Hue's city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Imperial Citadel of Hue (Hue Royal Citadel) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty (~200,000 VND entry). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Forbidden Purple City, ornate gates, and royal temples.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Perfume River promenade at sunset. Explore Dong Ba Market for local crafts, conical hats (non la), and street snacks. Evening cyclo ride around the citadel walls (~100,000–150,000 VND for 30 min).

meals.breakfast: Quick banh mi or xoi (sticky rice) from a street cart near the Old Quarter hotel before departing Hanoi.
meals.lunch: Banh Beo Chen at a local Hue restaurant — steamed rice cakes with shrimp and crispy pork skin, a Hue specialty, ~50,000–70,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Com Hen Hue (baby clam rice) at a riverside stall near Dong Ba Market — a legendary Hue street food dish, ~40,000–60,000 VND. Follow with Banh Khoai (Hue sizzling crepe) from a street vendor, ~30,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Flying is strongly recommended over the train for this leg to save a full day. Book flights 1–2 weeks in advance for best mid-range prices. Hue is the culinary capital of Vietnam — be adventurous with every meal here.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike (~150,000 VND/day) or hire a xe om (motorbike taxi) for a Royal Tombs tour south of Hue. Visit the Tomb of Tu Duc (most scenic, ~100,000 VND) and the Tomb of Minh Mang (~100,000 VND) — both set in pine forests along the Perfume River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Thien Mu Pagoda — Hue's most iconic seven-tiered pagoda perched on a hill above the Perfume River (free entry). Take a dragon boat cruise back along the Perfume River to the city center (~150,000–200,000 VND per person). Stop at a local lacquerware workshop to watch artisans at work.
day_by_day.evening: Join a Hue Royal Cuisine cooking class or food tour (~400,000–600,000 VND) led by a local guide through the backstreets. Learn about the refined, complex flavors of imperial Hue cooking.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong (a Hue branch) or local pho bo Hue — Hue-style spicy beef noodle soup (bun bo Hue), ~50,000–70,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Banh Canh Cua (thick noodle soup with crab) from a street stall near Dong Ba Market, ~50,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Truong Tien Bridge area night food stalls — try nem lui (lemongrass skewers), banh uot (steamed rice rolls), and fresh spring rolls. Budget ~100,000–150,000 VND for a street food feast.

day_by_day.notes: Hue's royal tombs are spread out — a motorbike or guided tour is the most efficient way to visit. April weather in Hue can be hot and humid; carry water. The cooking class is a highlight — book ahead via your guesthouse or Airbnb Experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a bus or hire a private car (split cost with other travelers) over the spectacular Hai Van Pass to Hoi An (~3.5 hours, ~200,000–400,000 VND). Stop at the pass summit for panoramic views of Da Nang Bay. Optionally stop briefly in Da Nang to see the Dragon Bridge before continuing to Hoi An.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a mid-range guesthouse in or near Hoi An Ancient Town. Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot — visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (Lai Vien Kieu), the Assembly Halls (Phuc Kien is the most ornate, ~120,000 VND), and the Old Town streets lined with yellow lanterns.
day_by_day.evening: Join the magical Hoi An lantern-lit Ancient Town at dusk — the town glows with hundreds of silk lanterns after sunset. Buy a floating lantern (~20,000–30,000 VND) and release it on the Thu Bon River for good luck.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong on Phan Chau Trinh Street, Hoi An — Anthony Bourdain called it the 'best banh mi in the world.' ~35,000–50,000 VND.
meals.lunch: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Vac) at White Rose Restaurant — a Hoi An exclusive dish made by a single family, ~80,000–100,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Cao Lau at Thanh Cao Lau Restaurant — Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish with pork and local herbs, made with water from a specific ancient well, ~60,000–80,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Cao Lau is unique to Hoi An and cannot be authentically replicated elsewhere in Vietnam — do not miss it. The Ancient Town charges an entry fee (~120,000 VND) which includes access to 5 heritage sites. Hoi An is extremely walkable and bike-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–70,000 VND/day) and cycle 4 km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach for a relaxed morning swim and beachside breakfast. April weather in Hoi An is generally warm and sunny — one of the best beach months.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town for a half-day tailoring experience — Hoi An is famous for custom-made clothing at affordable prices. Visit Yaly Couture or A Dong Silk for quality tailoring (~300,000–800,000 VND for a custom dress or shirt, ready in 24–48 hours). Explore the village of Tra Que Herb Village (~3 km from town) by bicycle — participate in a short farming activity (~150,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Take a cooking class at the Morning Glory Cooking School (~600,000–800,000 VND) — includes a market tour, hands-on cooking of 4–5 Hoi An dishes, and dinner with your creations. One of the best cooking experiences in Southeast Asia.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit, yogurt, and Vietnamese iced coffee at a beachside café at An Bang Beach, ~60,000–80,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Com Ga Hoi An (Hoi An chicken rice) at Com Ga Ba Buoi on Phan Chau Trinh Street — another Hoi An signature dish, ~60,000–80,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Included in the cooking class. Otherwise, try Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with pork and shrimp) at a local restaurant, ~50,000–70,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class 1–2 days in advance. Order tailored clothing on Day 6 evening or Day 7 morning to allow 48 hours for completion before departure. An Bang Beach has calmer waters than Cua Dai.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a bus or sleeper bus (~200,000–350,000 VND) or fly from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Flying takes 1 hour (~500,000–900,000 VND). Check into a mid-range guesthouse in District 1 (Bui Vien Street area or Ben Thanh area).
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation walk around District 1. Visit Ben Thanh Market — browse the indoor market for spices, coffee, and handicrafts (bargain hard — prices start 2–3x higher than fair value). Walk along Dong Khoi Street to the Notre-Dame Cathedral of Saigon and the Central Post Office (free entry, stunning French colonial architecture).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bui Vien Walking Street (Saigon's famous backpacker street) for an energetic evening — neon lights, live music, street food, and cold beers. Alternatively, rooftop bar at Chill Skybar or The Deck for cocktails with city views (~150,000–300,000 VND per drink).

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick banh mi or pho before departing Hoi An/Da Nang.
meals.lunch: Bun Thit Nuong (grilled pork vermicelli) from a street stall near Ben Thanh Market, ~60,000–80,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Nha Hang Ngon (260 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia) — a beautiful villa restaurant with dozens of Vietnamese regional dishes cooked in open-air stalls. Budget ~150,000–250,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh City is chaotic, loud, and thrilling — embrace the energy. Traffic is intense; cross streets slowly and steadily, never stopping. Keep valuables secure on Bui Vien Street. The flying option from Da Nang saves a full day compared to the bus.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (entry ~40,000 VND) — one of the most powerful and sobering museums in Southeast Asia, documenting the Vietnam-American War through photographs and artifacts. Allow 2 hours. Then visit the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) — the former South Vietnamese presidential palace, frozen in time since April 30, 1975.
day_by_day.afternoon: Half-day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~40 km northwest of HCMC). Join a group tour (~350,000–500,000 VND including transport) or take a bus independently. Crawl through the narrow wartime tunnels used by Viet Cong soldiers — a remarkable and claustrophobic piece of history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to District 1 by 6–7 PM. Explore the Saigon street food scene on a self-guided walk or join a street food tour (~400,000–600,000 VND) through District 1 and District 4 alleys, tasting 6–8 dishes.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Huynh Hoa on Le Thi Rieng Street — considered Saigon's finest banh mi, loaded with premium fillings, ~45,000–60,000 VND. Arrive early as queues form.
meals.lunch: Pho Hung on Nguyen Trai Street — outstanding Saigon-style pho with a richer, sweeter broth than Hanoi's version, ~70,000–90,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Street food crawl in District 4 — try Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes), Goi Cuon (fresh spring rolls), and Hu Tieu (Saigon noodle soup). Budget ~100,000–150,000 VND for multiple dishes.

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum contains graphic imagery — be mentally prepared. Cu Chi Tunnels Ben Dinh site is less touristy than Ben Duoc — ask your tour to go there. Book the street food tour in advance via Airbnb Experiences or Klook.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Vietnam. Visit the vibrant Binh Tay Market in Cholon (Chinatown, District 5) — Saigon's wholesale market, more authentic and less touristy than Ben Thanh. Explore the ornate Thien Hau Temple nearby (free entry) — a stunning 19th-century Cantonese pagoda filled with incense coils.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to District 1 for last-minute souvenir shopping at the Night Market (even open in the afternoon) or along Dong Khoi Street. Pick up Vietnamese coffee (Trung Nguyen brand), pho spice kits, silk scarves, or lacquerware. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner before heading to Tan Son Nhat International Airport. Allow 2–3 hours before departure for check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Ga (sticky rice with chicken) from a street cart near your guesthouse — a classic Vietnamese breakfast, ~40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Dim Sum lunch in Cholon at a local Cantonese restaurant near Binh Tay Market — a unique Vietnamese-Chinese fusion experience, ~100,000–150,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Cuc Gach Quan (District 3) — a charming, rustic Vietnamese home-cooking restaurant in a converted old house. Try the clay pot dishes and fresh tofu. Budget ~200,000–300,000 VND per person. Reserve a table in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Cholon is best explored by Grab or motorbike taxi — it's about 5–6 km from District 1. The Cuc Gach Quan restaurant is beloved by both locals and travelers — it's a perfect final meal to cap the trip. Leave at least 2.5 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in. Vietnam departure tax is included in most international tickets.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 – no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to Boutique Stay in the Old Quarter, Hanoi. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your heritage-style room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the iconic 36 Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore the labyrinthine alleyways, admire French-colonial architecture, and browse artisan shops selling silk, lacquerware, and handcrafted goods. Visit Hoan Kiem Lake and the iconic red Huc Bridge leading to Ngoc Son Temple for a serene first glimpse of Hanoi's soul.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the pedestrianised Dinh Le and Le Thai To streets as the city lights up. Experience the legendary Hanoi street food scene with a curated private street food tour of the Old Quarter – savour Bun Cha (grilled pork noodles), Banh Mi, and fresh Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric fish) at iconic local stalls.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or post-arrival light snack at hotel welcome)
meals.lunch: Premium welcome lunch at The Sofitel Legend Metropole's Le Club Bar – classic Vietnamese Pho Bo with premium beef cuts and herbal accompaniments
meals.dinner: Private guided street food tour dinner in the Old Quarter – curated tasting of Hanoi's finest street dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Cuon, and Bia Hoi (fresh draught beer) at a rooftop corner spot on Ta Hien Street

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance with your boutique hotel. April weather in Hanoi is warm and humid (~28°C) with occasional light showers – carry a light umbrella. Exchange some VND at the airport for street food purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a traditional Vietnamese breakfast at a celebrated Old Quarter café. Then embark on a private guided cultural tour of the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) – Vietnam's first university, dating to 1070. Explore its five courtyards, stone steles of doctoral graduates, and beautifully manicured gardens with an expert historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology, one of Southeast Asia's finest cultural museums, showcasing the 54 ethnic groups of Vietnam through immersive exhibits and outdoor reconstructed village structures. Followed by a visit to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex and the Presidential Palace gardens (exterior viewing and One Pillar Pagoda).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a world-renowned Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre performance – an ancient Vietnamese art form depicting folklore and rural life on water. Reserve premium front-row seats. Afterwards, enjoy a sophisticated dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking Hoan Kiem Lake.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong-style gourmet breakfast at Café Giang (birthplace of Egg Coffee) – try the iconic Ca Phe Trung (egg coffee) alongside fresh Xoi (sticky rice)
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at KOTO Restaurant (Know One Teach One) – a social enterprise fine-dining experience offering refined Vietnamese cuisine in a stylish French villa setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Badiane – award-winning French-Vietnamese fusion restaurant in a restored colonial mansion; try the tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays and has a strict dress code (no shorts or sleeveless tops). Water puppet theatre tickets should be booked in advance. Comfortable walking shoes recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the ancient village of Bat Trang Ceramic Village (~45 min from Old Quarter by private car). Explore centuries-old kilns, watch master potters at work, and participate in a hands-on premium pottery workshop. Browse and purchase bespoke hand-painted ceramics as unique souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hanoi and visit Hoa Lo Prison (the 'Hanoi Hilton') for a sobering and historically rich cultural experience. Then explore the vibrant Dong Xuan Market – Hanoi's largest covered market – for premium Vietnamese silks, spices, and local goods with a personal shopping guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a premium rooftop bar in the Old Quarter (Cama ATK Rooftop or Summit Lounge at the Pan Pacific) with panoramic views over the Hanoi skyline. Dinner at a celebrated Vietnamese fine-dining establishment specialising in Northern Vietnamese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) breakfast at the legendary Pho Gia Truyen on Bat Dan Street – a Hanoi institution since 1955, beloved by locals and gourmands alike
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional family-run restaurant in Bat Trang Village – fresh clay-pot fish and seasonal vegetables prepared in traditional Northern Vietnamese style
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cha Ca Thang Long – Hanoi's most celebrated Cha Ca restaurant, serving the signature sizzling turmeric-marinated catfish with dill, peanuts, and vermicelli noodles

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private car transfer to Bat Trang through your hotel concierge. Bring cash for market shopping. April evenings are pleasant for rooftop dining – light layers recommended after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanoi by luxury private transfer (3.5 hours) to Ha Long Bay. En route, stop at a premium lacquerware and silk workshop in the countryside. Board your private luxury overnight cruise vessel at the Ha Long Bay International Cruise Port. Welcome champagne reception and safety briefing on deck as you sail into the UNESCO World Heritage-listed bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cruise through the emerald waters of Ha Long Bay, passing thousands of towering limestone karsts. Visit the spectacular Thien Cung (Heavenly Palace) Cave with expert geological commentary. Kayaking or bamboo boat excursion through hidden lagoons and sea caves inaccessible to larger vessels.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the sun deck as the karsts glow golden at dusk. Premium multi-course seafood dinner prepared by the onboard chef using freshly caught local seafood – lobster, crab, prawns, and seasonal fish with Vietnamese herb accompaniments. Stargazing from the deck.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at your Hanoi boutique hotel before departure – Vietnamese rice porridge (Chao), fresh tropical fruits, pastries, and Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch onboard the luxury cruise – freshly prepared Vietnamese spring rolls, grilled squid, steamed clams, and rice with panoramic bay views
meals.dinner: Onboard premium seafood dinner – five-course tasting menu featuring Ha Long Bay lobster thermidor, steamed crab with ginger and spring onion, and Vietnamese dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Pack light for the cruise – a small overnight bag is sufficient (main luggage can be stored at your Hanoi hotel). Bring sunscreen, a hat, and swimwear. Choose a luxury cruise line such as Paradise Elegance, Indochine Sails, or Au Co Cruise for the finest experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Tai Chi session on the sun deck at sunrise, guided by the cruise wellness instructor. Post-breakfast, visit a traditional floating fishing village (Cua Van or Vung Vieng) by bamboo boat – meet local fishermen and learn about their centuries-old way of life. Optional pearl farm visit to learn about Ha Long's cultured pearl industry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return cruise to port (arriving approximately 12:30). Private luxury transfer to Cat Ba Island (or return to Hanoi depending on preference). If returning to Hanoi, afternoon at leisure for spa treatment at your boutique hotel or independent Old Quarter exploration. Alternatively, check into a premium Cat Ba Island resort for an extended bay experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by private car. Relaxed evening in the Old Quarter – explore the night market (open Friday to Sunday) or enjoy a traditional Vietnamese massage at a premium wellness spa such as Moc Huong Spa or La Belle Spa.

meals.breakfast: Full Vietnamese and Western breakfast buffet onboard the cruise ship – Pho, Banh Mi, tropical fruits, eggs, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch onboard before disembarkation – Vietnamese fried rice with seafood, fresh salads, and fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Quan An Ngon Hanoi – a premium open-air restaurant recreating the best street food stalls from across Vietnam in an elegant colonial courtyard setting

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return transfer timing with cruise operator the evening before. If visiting on a weekend, the Old Quarter night market (Hang Dao to Dong Xuan) is a must-visit experience. Book spa treatments in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Hanoi (Noi Bai) to Hoi An via Da Nang (approx. 1.5-hour flight – book in advance on Vietnam Airlines or Bamboo Airways business class). Private luxury transfer from Da Nang Airport to Hoi An Ancient Town (~45 minutes). Check into a premium riverside resort or heritage boutique hotel in or near the Ancient Town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided walking tour of Hoi An Ancient Town (UNESCO World Heritage Site) – visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, Phung Hung Ancient House, Tan Ky Old House, and the Assembly Halls of the Fujian and Cantonese Chinese communities. Explore the vibrant tailoring district and commission bespoke Vietnamese clothing.
day_by_day.evening: As dusk falls, the Ancient Town transforms into a magical lantern-lit wonderland. Join a private lantern-making workshop with a local artisan family, then release a lotus lantern onto the Thu Bon River. Dinner at a premium restaurant on the riverside promenade.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or post-arrival light lunch (see below)
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at Morning Glory Restaurant – Hoi An's most celebrated restaurant by chef Trinh Diem Vy, specialising in authentic Central Vietnamese cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Deck House or Mango Rooms – upscale riverside dining with refined Vietnamese and fusion cuisine; try the White Rose Dumplings (Banh Vac) and Cao Lau noodles, dishes unique to Hoi An

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An's Ancient Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle. Entrance tickets are required for most heritage houses (purchase a combo ticket). April is a warm, relatively dry month in Hoi An – ideal conditions. Commission tailored clothing early (allow 24–48 hours for completion).

day_by_day.morning: Private premium cooking class with a renowned Hoi An chef – begin with a guided tour of the Central Market to source fresh ingredients (herbs, spices, exotic vegetables, fresh seafood), then learn to prepare five signature Central Vietnamese dishes including Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes), Mi Quang noodles, and Hoi An-style White Rose dumplings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the serene countryside surrounding Hoi An by private bicycle or electric bicycle – ride through emerald rice paddies, visit the ancient Tra Que Herb Village, and interact with local farmers. Enjoy a traditional herbal foot massage at the village using freshly harvested herbs. Return to town and collect any bespoke tailored clothing ordered the previous day.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise along the Thu Bon River on a private decorated wooden vessel with cocktails and canapés. Disembark at An Bang Beach for an evening beach walk. Dinner at a premium beachside restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel – fresh tropical fruit platter, Vietnamese drip coffee, Banh Mi, and local specialties
meals.lunch: Cooking class lunch – enjoy the dishes you prepared during the morning class in a beautiful garden setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Soul Kitchen (An Bang Beach) or Saltwater Restaurant – sophisticated beach-side dining with fresh grilled seafood, wood-fired dishes, and craft cocktails under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance through your hotel concierge – classes at Red Bridge Cooking School or Thuan Tinh Island are highly recommended. Bring comfortable clothes for cycling. An Bang Beach is approximately 5km from the Ancient Town – arrange a tuk-tuk or private car for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to the majestic My Son Sanctuary (~45 minutes from Hoi An) – a UNESCO World Heritage Site comprising ancient Cham Hindu temple ruins dating from the 4th to 14th centuries. Explore with a specialist archaeologist guide for an in-depth understanding of the Champa Kingdom's history and architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An and visit the Hoi An Museum of Folk Culture and the Museum of Trade Ceramics for deeper cultural immersion. Afternoon at leisure for spa treatment at your resort – many premium Hoi An resorts offer traditional Vietnamese herbal treatments and Cham-inspired therapies.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Hoi An – immerse yourself in the Full Moon Lantern Festival atmosphere (or a regular evening if not full moon). Stroll the lantern-lit Ancient Town streets, browse the night market for premium silk lanterns and handicrafts, and enjoy a farewell dinner at Hoi An's finest fine-dining establishment.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel – Chao (rice porridge with ginger and shallots), fresh fruit, Vietnamese coffee, and pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional Cham-inspired restaurant near My Son or a picnic lunch prepared by your hotel
meals.dinner: Farewell Hoi An dinner at The Field Restaurant (Anantara Hoi An Resort) or Cargo Club Restaurant – multi-course Vietnamese tasting menu with wine pairing in an exquisitely restored colonial building

day_by_day.notes: My Son is best visited early morning to avoid heat and crowds – depart by 08:00 if possible. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sun protection. Confirm flight details for the following day's travel to Ho Chi Minh City.

day_by_day.morning: Morning flight from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Son Nhat Airport) – approximately 1.5 hours (business class). Private luxury transfer to a premium hotel in District 1 (Saigon). Check-in and freshen up. Begin exploration of the French Quarter – visit the iconic Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica, the Central Post Office (designed by Gustave Eiffel), and the Reunification Palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided cultural tour of the War Remnants Museum – a powerful and moving museum documenting the Vietnam War through photographs and artefacts. Visit the historic Ben Thanh Market for premium Vietnamese handicrafts, spices, and street food tastings. Explore the upscale Dong Khoi Street for luxury Vietnamese silk, art galleries, and designer boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails at the Chill Skybar (AB Tower) or the iconic rooftop of the Hotel Majestic overlooking the Saigon River. Dinner at a celebrated Ho Chi Minh City restaurant specialising in Southern Vietnamese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final Hoi An breakfast at your resort before airport transfer – full Vietnamese breakfast spread
meals.lunch: Lunch at Propaganda Bistro (District 1) – acclaimed Vietnamese bistro with bold flavours, vintage propaganda-inspired décor, and a creative take on Southern Vietnamese classics
meals.dinner: Dinner at Noir. Dining in the Dark – a unique premium dining experience served in complete darkness by visually impaired staff, featuring a sophisticated Vietnamese tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) is significantly hotter and more energetic than Hanoi – expect temperatures around 33–35°C in April. Stay hydrated. District 1 is walkable but taxis or Grab (ride-hailing) are recommended for longer distances. Book Noir restaurant well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early private guided excursion to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~1.5 hours from Saigon) – explore the extraordinary 250km network of underground tunnels used during the Vietnam War. Opt for the premium Ben Duoc section (less crowded than Ben Dinh) with an expert historian guide. Crawl through sections of the tunnels and visit a traditional Cu Chi craft workshop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Saigon for a final afternoon of exploration. Visit the vibrant Binh Tay Market in Cholon (Saigon's historic Chinatown district) – a sensory feast of spices, dried goods, and authentic street life. Explore the ornate Thien Hau Pagoda. Final souvenir shopping at premium artisan boutiques on Le Loi and Dong Khoi Streets.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Saigon's finest rooftop fine-dining restaurants. Final stroll along the Nguyen Hue Walking Street – Saigon's grand pedestrian boulevard. Private luxury transfer to Tan Son Nhat Airport for departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel – Banh Mi Saigon-style (pork pâté, cold cuts, pickled vegetables), fresh tropical fruit, Ca Phe Sua Da (Vietnamese iced coffee with condensed milk)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Com Nieu Saigon – a legendary Saigon institution famous for its clay-pot rice (Com Nieu) smashed open tableside, with an array of Southern Vietnamese dishes
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Anan Saigon (rooftop) – Chef Peter Cuong Franklin's acclaimed modern Vietnamese restaurant blending street food heritage with fine-dining innovation; try the Pho Wagyu Beef Tasting or the signature Banh Mi 23 with premium toppings

day_by_day.notes: Cu Chi Tunnels trip should depart by 07:30 to return comfortably for afternoon activities. Confirm departure flight time and arrange airport transfer accordingly – allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Pack bespoke tailored clothing and ceramics carefully. Keep premium purchases in carry-on luggage where possible.
